**Evidence:** [[AIClinicalValidationInDrugDiscovery]], [[CancerImmuneRecognitionProblem]], [[CancerVaccinePlatform]], [[IndividualizedCancerVaccine]], [[IndividualizedCancerVaccineManufacturing]], [[NeoantigenSelectionTradeoff]], [[RecurrenceFreeSurvivalEndpoint]], [[TumorMicroenvironment]], [[Moderna]], [[Merck]], [[InterPath001]], [[YingBo]], [[AiboShengwu]], [[vol-220-duihua-dabainiu-under-modena-dingzhi-kangai-yimiao-li-putongren-you-duoyuan-lofs520ps1evva8nafsnrkcbvgjz]], [[e250-mrna-de-dier-zhanchang-duihua-yingbo-chaijie-moderna-renlei-shouge-zhongliu-yimiao-sanqi-tupo-73a69583-98ee-43d6-a892-3e7c93012dd9]], [[all-in-with-chamath-jason-sacks-friedberg-nvidias-historic-quarter-saas-comeback-bessent-vs-druck-americas-debt-crisis-cancer-vaccine-42597345]], [[CancerImmunotherapyAccess]]

**Qualifications:**

- The evidence is concentrated in melanoma postoperative adjuvant therapy and should not be generalized to every cancer, preventive vaccine, or tumor setting.
- AI is framed as workflow acceleration for neoantigen prediction, sequence optimization, and possibly delivery design, not as a substitute for locked clinical processes, endpoint evidence, safety, and medical judgment.
- E250 treats the InterPath001 phase 3 RFS result as stronger platform validation, but HR/subgroups, OS, approval, cost, access, and manufacturing scale remain unresolved.
- The new All-In cancer-vaccine segment adds that access, patents, charged price, possible lower production cost, right-to-try routes, and non-mRNA implementation paths remain distinct from the biological neoantigen thesis.
